subject: setting the axes for a graph

messages.author: 496499cefe2ae056
messages.subject: setting the axes for a graph
parts:
Hi,

I created what many would consider to be an unusual plot -- it's
strictly text. I very often do this in S-Plus when I want nice looking
summary tables to accompany a typical graph such as a bar chart. I now
want to do this using gglot2. I set the axes to be 0:1 using

p <- ggplot( data = NULL )
p <- p + xlim( 0, 1 ) + ylim( 0, 1 ) + xlab( "" ) + ylab ( "" )

and then followed this with a number of geom_text statements to give me
the table I want. I would imagine that the axes would always be 0:1,
and they are. But what appears on the screen varies from, say, 0:0.65,
or some other number, and not 0:1. Actually, the y-axis is ok; it's the
x-axis that gets distorted and truncated. This means that when I copy
the text plot to PowerPoint, the whole plot (i.e., summary table) is
distorted and doesn't show everything, even though the axes are both
suppose to be 0:1. How can I get the plot area to show as 0:1 on the
screen and when copied when I set them to be 0:1? I don't want ggplot
to change anything.

Thanks,

Walt

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: setting the axes for a graph
parts:
Hi:

A useful place to look would be the gridExtra package, particularly
the function tableGrob(). Try out the examples to get a feel for what
it does. If your intention is to combine a table with one or more
plots, you should also look at the grid.arrange() function in the same
package. gridExtra plays nice with grid graphics, which includes both
ggplot2 and lattice.

HTH,
Dennis
